tips: Load Suica to Apple/Google Wallet while waiting at the MSP gate — land already armed for transit.
Set phones to JST and take melatonin at 13:00 CT (≈ 4am JST) to start aligning your clock before the 14-hour leg.

2026-12-15.weatherAlert: December evenings in Tokyo are cold (often near freezing). Dress in layers for the Omoide Yokocho outdoor seating and Kabukicho neon walk.
tips: Hit the Limousine Bus counter at Haneda before the ATM — buses accept IC cards or cash and sell out slower than trains fill up.
Jet-lag crash protocol: anyone hitting the wall hands their konbini order to a squadmate and sleeps without shame.

2026-12-16.weatherAlert: High rain risk for an outdoor-heavy day. Meiji Shrine, Harajuku, and the Blue Cave illumination are all exposed.

suggestedSwap.originalActivity: Shibuya Blue Cave illumination — ~600k blue LEDs toward Yoyogi
suggestedSwap.suggestedAlt: Miyashita Park covered rooftop + Parco + Tower Records (9 floors) absorb a full wet afternoon without surfacing.
suggestedSwap.reason: The Blue Cave illumination walk is entirely outdoors and miserable in cold December rain; Miyashita Park and Parco offer covered, weather-proof alternatives.

tips: Shibuya Sky sunset slots sell out fast — book immediately upon arrival if the crew is set on it, or pivot to Mag's Park rooftop.
If day one cooked the crew, swap the late Blue Cave walk for an early nomihodai and 23:00 lights-out.

2026-12-17.weatherAlert: Cold, dry December day. The Senso-ji and Nakamise morning walk is fully exposed; dress warmly.
tips: Arrive at Senso-ji before 08:30 to beat the crowds — the Nakamise stalls open early and the main hall is peaceful.
If the Tokyo Skytree queue is insane, pivot to the Asahi Beer Hall's 22F Sky Room next door for the same river view for the price of a beer.

2026-12-18.crowdAlert: teamLab Planets requires the Sept 18 booking; absolutely no walk-ins. Golden Gai bars are tiny — a group of 8 will need to split across 2-3 bars.
tips: Tsukiji Outer Market stalls start closing around 14:00 — go early for the freshest sushi breakfast.
For Golden Gai, split into 2-3 smaller groups to fit inside the tiny 6-seat bars and avoid cover charges for large parties.

2026-12-19.weatherAlert: Rain risk for the coastal Kamakura/Enoshima day trip. The Enoden coastal tram views and Fuji-over-Sagami-Bay sunset are easily obscured by clouds or rain.

suggestedSwap.originalActivity: Enoshima island — climb to the Sea Candle
suggestedSwap.suggestedAlt: Enoshima onsen finish: Enospa overlooks the bay — soak with a Fuji view before the train if legs are cooked.
suggestedSwap.reason: Climbing Enoshima in cold December rain is exposed and slippery; Enospa provides a warm, weather-proof alternative with bay views.

tips: If it's raining heavily, skip the Fuji sunset view and head back to Shinjuku earlier for a cozy gyukatsu dinner.
The Enoden tram gets very crowded on weekends; try to board at the first stop (Kamakura station) to secure seats.

2026-12-20.weatherAlert: Rain risk for the outdoor Inokashira Park morning walk.

suggestedSwap.suggestedAlt: Ikebukuro Sunshine City — 3,000-machine gachapon hall + Pokémon Center MEGA under one roof.
suggestedSwap.reason: Inokashira Park is unpleasant in cold December rain; Sunshine City offers a massive indoor alternative for the morning.

tips: Run the Airbnb washer during dinner so everyone lands in Kyoto with a clean kit.
Pack FIRST before heading out for the Golden Gai encore — bags must close tonight for the morning shinkansen.

2026-12-21.weatherAlert: Rain risk for the Gion golden hour walk and Kamo River nightcaps, which are fully exposed to the elements.

suggestedSwap.originalActivity: Gion at golden hour — Hanamikoji + Shirakawa canal
suggestedSwap.suggestedAlt: Kyoto International Manga Museum — 50,000 manga, huge English wall, a school where you just sit and read.
suggestedSwap.reason: Gion's charm relies on atmospheric outdoor strolling, which is ruined in cold December rain; the Manga Museum is a perfect indoor time-vortex alternative.

tips: Grab ekiben at Tokyo Station's Ekibenya Matsuri before boarding — the Nozomi doesn't have great food carts.
Sit on the LEFT side (Seat E) of the Nozomi for the Fuji view around minute 40 of the ride.

2026-12-22.weatherAlert: Rain risk for the Fushimi Inari dawn hike and Kiyomizu-dera outdoor wooden stage.

suggestedSwap.originalActivity: Kiyomizu-dera — the wooden stage over the valley
suggestedSwap.suggestedAlt: Sanjusangendo — 1,001 golden Kannon statues in a 120m hall. Indoor, jaw-dropping, criminally underrated.
suggestedSwap.reason: Kiyomizu-dera's iconic views are obscured in rain, and the wooden stage is slippery; Sanjusangendo is entirely indoors and spectacular in any weather.

tips: Start Fushimi Inari before 07:00 to beat the crowds — past Yotsutsuji the crowds hit zero.
Vending machine hot corn soup on the descent is a December lifesaver.

2026-12-23.weatherAlert: Rain risk for the Arashiyama Bamboo Grove and Nara deer park, which offer zero shelter.

suggestedSwap.originalActivity: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove before the buses exist
suggestedSwap.suggestedAlt: Kimono Forest at Randen Arashiyama station: pillar-lit fabric columns glowing at dusk — free, on the way out anyway.
suggestedSwap.reason: The Bamboo Grove offers no canopy and is cold/dreary in December rain; the Kimono Forest is a quick, visually striking outdoor alternative that doesn't require a long exposed walk.

tips: Wakakusa-yama climb is CLOSED for our entire trip (closes second Sunday of December) — do not attempt it.
Bow to the deer first and show empty hands when done; never run, as they read it as a game they will win.

2026-12-24.crowdAlert: Christmas Eve in Dotonbori will be extremely crowded. KFC Christmas buckets often require pre-ordering in Japan; walk-ins may face multi-hour waits.
tips: If you haven't pre-ordered your KFC Christmas bucket, pivot to a local konbini fried chicken bucket — it's equally festive and zero wait.
Uji matcha shops close around 17:00; ensure you finish the Nintendo Museum and matcha pilgrimage before heading to Osaka.

2026-12-25.crowdAlert: USJ will be at peak Christmas capacity. Super Nintendo World timed entry is fiercely contested; rope-drop is mandatory.
tips: Use single-rider lines for Mario Kart and Forbidden Journey to cut 60% off wait times if Express Passes aren't held.
If Kinopio's Café is full, the Yoshi snack stand + popcorn buckets + Power-Up Band challenges still deliver the serotonin.

2026-12-26.weatherAlert: Rain risk for Miyajima Island. The floating torii gate views and outdoor oyster grills are exposed to the elements.
tips: This is the longest day of the trip — anyone redlining should skip Miyajima, do the Peace Museum unhurried, and meet at Hiroshima station.
Shukkei-en garden is a quiet 10-minute walk from the station if the museum hits heavy and you need a peaceful breather.

2026-12-27.weatherAlert: Rain risk for the 4km Midosuji Illumination walk and Umeda Sky Building outdoor Floating Garden.

suggestedSwap.originalActivity: UMEDA SKY BUILDING — sunset from the Floating Garden
suggestedSwap.suggestedAlt: Abeno Harukas — Japan's tallest building (300m) with fully indoor observation decks.
suggestedSwap.reason: The Umeda Sky Building's Floating Garden is largely exposed and dangerously windy in cold December rain; Abeno Harukas offers a warmer, fully indoor sunset alternative.

tips: Buy 551 Horai butaman 4-packs from Namba station BEFORE the crab dinner — they sell out nightly.
If 13 days of walking have collected their tax, pivot to Spa World in Shinsekai for a gloriously kitsch recovery bath.

2026-12-28.weatherAlert: Rain risk for the outdoor Himeji Castle complex and Kobe Harborland.

suggestedSwap.originalActivity: Kitano Ijinkan district — 19th-century merchant mansions on the hill
suggestedSwap.suggestedAlt: Nada sake district audible: Hakutsuru brewery museum (free, tastings) is two stops from Sannomiya.
suggestedSwap.reason: The Kitano Ijinkan district requires a steep outdoor walk up the hill, which is miserable in cold December rain; the Hakutsuru brewery museum is indoor, warm, and features free sake tastings.

tips: Check tax-free paperwork tonight: receipts with passports, purchases accessible — customs CAN ask on exit.
If Kobe beef lunch at a sit-down restaurant breaks the budget, the $22 (¥3,500) Kobe-beef bowls and croquette stands around Sannomiya deliver 70% of the experience at 40% of the price.
Sit on the LEFT side (Seat A) of the Nozomi for Fuji's encore on the ride back to Tokyo.
Use any remaining Suica balance on final boss gachapon or a last airside meal — international transit doesn't easily allow refunds.

globalTips: With the USD/JPY rate at ~161.68, your dollar stretches far in Japan. Withdraw large sums from 7-Eleven ATMs to avoid per-transaction fees, and pay with IC cards (Suica) for transit and konbini runs to skip cash-counting.
December in Japan is cold and dry, with occasional rain. Pack versatile layers, a solid rain shell, and comfortable walking shoes—avoid cotton sneakers that soak through on wet temple steps.
For a group of 8, always split into 2-3 smaller squads when entering tiny bars (Golden Gai, Pontocho, Ura-Namba) or crowded restaurants to ensure seating and avoid cover charges.
